title: Kitchener Indoor Recreation Complex design and budget approved
subtitle: Also: dog designation appeals, Victoria Street North development deferred, Bramm Street parking hours, heritage designations and community grants.
overview: Council approved an upgraded design and a total budget of $143,820,000 for the Kitchener Indoor Recreation Complex {{vote:m1}}. The facility will have a larger FIFA-sized indoor turf field, a bigger leisure pool, an elevated walking track and an indoor cricket batting cage. It will be built as the City's first net-zero carbon facility. Additional debenture financing of $47,915,000 will be repaid from future development charge revenue, and speakers said this means no direct cost to property taxpayers.

Council ratified the dog designation appeal decisions, with one amendment. Meeko's designation is Potentially Dangerous Dog, and Broly's Dangerous Dog designation stands, both with modified conditions. It also deferred a decision on a large development at 236-264 Victoria Street North to a special meeting before April 19, so the applicant can talk further with an existing commercial tenant.

Bramm Street surface parking will go back to its pre-2024 hours, Monday to Saturday, 8 am to 5 pm, while the City reviews downtown parking. Council also approved Tier 2 community grants, heritage designation notices for two properties, and three environmental assessments.

decisions.detail: Council approved the expanded design, net-zero carbon approach, a total budget of $143,820,000, extra debenture financing of $47,915,000 and the construction-phase agreement with the IPD team.
Council ratified the appeal committee decisions, keeping the Dangerous Dog designation for Broly and assigning Potentially Dangerous Dog for Meeko, both with modified conditions.
Council deferred the Official Plan and zoning amendments to a special meeting before April 19 so the applicant can speak further with an existing commercial tenant.
Bramm Street lot fees revert temporarily to the pre-2024 model, with a review of the downtown free-parking subsidy in 2024 and a new rate structure considered in the 2025 budget.
The Clerk will publish a Notice of Intention to Designate the property under the Ontario Heritage Act.
The Clerk will publish a Notice of Intention to Designate the property under the Ontario Heritage Act.
Council approved $209,415 in Tier 2 community grants.
Council approved the environmental study report, directed a 30-day public review, and directed detailed design and implementation of Stage 1 once the assessment is complete.

debate: Delegates from the Kitchener Soccer Club supported the recreation complex. They said the club has a waiting list, many families travel outside the city for winter training, and the current indoor facility is small and aging. They also said a year-round field would allow more tournaments.
Councillors said the recreation complex is funded by development charges rather than by property taxes. They also said the new project delivery approach has gone well so far.

In the dog appeals, the owner said there were mitigating factors, the incident happened on the owner's property, and sterilization would not reduce aggression. A dog behaviourist described Meeko as not dangerous. One councillor asked whether the appeal committee had heard this. Another councillor said it had not, and the owner had months before the hearing to present it.

On Victoria Street North, the applicant's planner offered 32 affordable units, about 3% of the total, and a commitment of no demolition or construction in the first five years of the tenant's lease. The planner said free dedicated parking for the tenant would cost millions. Staff said the City cannot enforce these commitments. A proposal to defer only until later that evening was defeated.

On Bramm Street, the sponsoring councillor said reverting the hours fits what residents expected when they moved in. Staff supported the change as a temporary step during the review. One councillor noted parking is running a deficit and said the City should not be in the business of providing parking for condos.
